newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala revises up 96-97 coffee export outlook.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala revises up 96-97 coffee export outlook.

text.p: Guatemala admitted Thursday that it has a larger coffee crop than originally thought and revised upward its export forecast accordingly, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said.

Julio Arrivillaga, Anacafe's president, said the Guatemala coffee harvest is almost finished and that Guatemala expects to export more than 1 million more bags from this harvest than the 2,738,401 60-kg bags already exported.
In January, Anacafe predicted exports of 3 million bags for the current harvest, down from 3.6 million bags exported during the 1995-1996 crop.

"We are going to export a million more (60-kilo bags) -- a larger harvest than what we had thought," Arrivillaga said. He said total exports during the current harvest could come close to 3.7 million bags.
"I'm thinking some coffee has come in from other countries, distorting our predictions, but I better not point any fingers," Arrivillaga said.

Contraband coffee is well known to flow in the Mexico and Central American region, distorting production and export figures. Different local tax regimes in the countries are blamed on the illegal trade.
